sentences.text: The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/S.166 of M.V. Act against the respondents claiming compensation amount of Rs.15,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are as under:
On 29.8.2017 at about 8.15 p.m. the petitioner was proceeding on a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-05-EZ- 2204 as a pillion rider and the rider R.Harsha was ridden his vehicle slowly, cautiously on the correct side of Bangarpete-Kolar road, on the way at about 8.15 p.m. near Karnataka Bank ATM, Kolar Town, at that time one Honda CB Shine Motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-07-V-3237 came from opposite direction with high speed in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and safety of others and dashed against the motor cycle.
As a result of the forced impact, the petitioner knocked down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately the petitioner was shifted to R.L.Jalappa Hospital, Kolar,
wherein petitioner took the treatment as inpatient.

3. Further the contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy,
aged about 19 years, bricks maker and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Honda CB Shine motor cycle bearing No.KA-07-V-3237.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Contending the above facts, he prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost.
4. In response to the petition notice, the respondents have appeared before the court and filed their written statement.
5. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 are as under:
The respondent No.1has contended in its written statement that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further contended that the accident not occurred due to the carelessness, rash and negligent riding of Honda CB Shine motor cycle.
Further denied the entire petition averments.
Contending the above facts, prays to dismiss the petition with costs.

6.The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 are as under:
The respondent No.1has contended in its written statement that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further this respondent has admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.
KA-07-V- 3237 and its validity.

Further contended that neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied the mandatory provisions of S.
134 and S. 158(6) of the M.V. Act in furnishing the better particulars.

Further contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the motor Shri J.Sarvana vs Shri Ashwatha Gowda on 25 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150170862/
2 cycle bearing No.KA-05-EZ-2204.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition.
Contending the above facts, he prays to dismiss the claim petition as against this respondent with cost.

7. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:
1.
Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-07-V-3237?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3.
What order or award?
8. In order to prove the case, the petitioner himself has examined as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P9 and doctor is examined as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P10 & Ex.P11.
9. To disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove the defence, the respondents have not examined any witness on its behalf.

10. Heard the arguments.
11.

My findings to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: In the Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per final order for the following:
R E A S O N S 12. ISSUE NO.1:- During the course of arguments, the learned counsel for the petitioner argued by reiterating the contents of petition and also evidence put forth by PW1 & PW2.
Further he argued that, to prove the disablement, the petitioner has examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW2, who has assessed the disability of left lower limb and 33% and whole body disability is 11%.
Further he argued that the petitioner has proved his case as contended in the petition by producing oral and documentary evidence.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.

13. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondents have denied the accident in toto, hence,
prays to dismiss the petition.
14. On rival contention urged by both the counsel, I, intend to discuss the merits of the case.

sentences.text: In order to prove the case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 and he has stated in his evidence by reiterating the contents of petition.

Further in support of his evidence, he has produced the prosecution papers and the same are marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P7 such as Police intimation, FIR with complaint, spot mahazar, rough sketch, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet.
16.
On perusal of Ex.P1 is the police intimation, Ex.P2 is the complaint reveals that complaint has been lodged by Ravi, son of Keshaval on 30.8.2017.

So, based on the complaint, FIR came to be registered by Kolar Traffic Police in Cr. No.74/2017 against the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-07-V- 3237 for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 337 of IPC.
Ex. P3
is the spot mahazar and Ex.P4 is the sketch also reveals the scene of occurrence and it corroborate the evidence of PW1.
Ex . P5
is the IMV report reveals that the damages caused to both the vehicles and IMV inspector has opined that the accident was not due to mechanical defect of the vehicle.
On perusal of Ex.P6-wound certificate reveals that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
Ex.P7 is the charge sheet reveals that after investigation I.O. has filed charge sheet against the rider of the motor cycle for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 338 of IPC R/w S.177 of IMV Act.
17. The counsel for the respondents have argued that the accident has not occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-07-V-3237.
But, to substantiate the said fact, the respondents have not led any rebuttal evidence in order to disprove the contention of the petitioner.
On the other hand petitioner has proved his case through oral and documentary evidence.

18. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others).

sentences.text: 19. Looking to the oral evidence of PW1 and the documents placed before the court, it is clear that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-07-V-3237.
Hence, I answer this issue in the affirmative.
20. ISSUE NO.2:-
The case of the petitioner is that he met with an accident on 29.8.2017 at about 8.15 p.m. and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to R.L.Jalappa Hospital,
Kolar, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient.

To substantiate the said fact, petitioner has produced wound certificate at Ex.P6, which discloses the following injuries;
Left Iliac wing fracture 21.
The doctor is of the opinion that the injury is grievous in nature.

The petitioner has produced copy of the discharge summary marked at Ex.P8, which discloses that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took the treatment as inpatient from 30.8.2017 to 13.9.2017.
Dr.Nagaraj B.N. has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained Left Iliac wing fracture.
He has produced Clinical examination note and X-ray marked at Ex.P10 & Ex.P11.

sentences.text: Considering the oral evidence of PW1 & PW2 and the documents placed before the court, I am of the opinion that the petitioner might have sustained pain and agony, for which, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.35,000/- under the head of pain and sufferings.
24. The case of the petitioner is that, he was hale and healthy at the time of accident, aged about 19 years, bricks maker and getting an income of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But he has not produced any documents pertains to his avocation and income.
In the absence of the documents pertains to his avocation and income, it is very difficult to assess the income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition.
So, considering the present life condition and the age of the petitioner, if notional income of Rs.7,500/- per month is considered, it will meet the ends of justice.

The petitioner has produced copy of the discharge summary marked at Ex.P8, which discloses that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took the treatment as inpatient from 30.8.2017 to 13.9.2017.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries; he might have taken rest and treatment at least for two months.
Therefore, two months income comes to Rs.14,000/- is granted to the petitioner under the head of loss of income during laid up period and rest period.
25. The contention of the petitioner is that, he has spent huge amount of Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses.
He has not produced any documents relating to the medical expenses incurred for his treatment.
So, no amount is granted under this head.
26. Further contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 19 years, Bricks maker and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the accident, he is completely bed ridden and lost his earnings.
27. To prove the age, the petitioner has produced Aadhar card marked at Ex.P9.
On perusal of the same, the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 5.4.1999 and the accident occurred on 29.8.2017.
So, as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged about 18 years.
So, same is considered as the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident.
28. PW2-Dr.Nagaraj B.N. has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and assessed the permanent disability.
According to him, the petitioner has 33% of left lower limb and 11% of whole body disability.

So, considering the evidence of PW2 and the cross-examination and the age and avocation of the petitioner and relative disability, if 8% is considered as whole body of disability of the petitioner, it will meet the ends of justice.
The petitioner age is already considered as 18 years the multiplier applicable to this age is 18.
Considering the above facts, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.1,29,600/- under the head of loss of future earning.
30. Further contention of the petitioner is that the petitioner has sustained fracture.
So his happiness and pleasure will be restricted to some extent through out his life.

Hence, it is just and Shri J.Sarvana vs Shri Ashwatha Gowda on 25 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150170862/
5 necessary to award compensation of Rs.5,000/- under the head of amenities.

sentences.text: 31. PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to the accident he took the treatment as inpatient.
He has produced the discharge summary marked at Ex.P8, which discloses that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took the treatment as inpatient from 30.8.2017 to 13.9.2017.
So, one must attend him during the above said period.

Considering the above facts and looking to the period of hospitalization, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.15,000/- under the head of attendant, conveyance, food and nourishment etc.
32.

Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:
 Sl.No. Compensation heads Amount  1. Pain and suffering Rs. 35,000-00 2. Loss of income during laid period Rs. 14,000-00 and rest period 3.
Medical expenses Nil 4. Loss of future income Rs.1,29,600-00 5. Loss of amenities, Rs. 5,000-00 6.
Attendant, Nourishment and Rs. 15,000-00 conveyance charges Total Rs.1,98,600-00 33.
LIABILITY:

On perusal of the contents of petition and contents of written statement, it reveals that, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-07-V-3237.
34.
The respondent No.2 has admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of motor cycle bearing No.KA-07-V-3237 and its validity.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 8% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 in partly affirmative.
35. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of above discussion on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of MV act is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,98,600/- with interest @ 8% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 8% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
